title: Configuring SAML Single Sign-On
content:
CyberArk Identity supports SAML 2.0 for single sign-on (SSO) integration with enterprise applications. This guide covers configuring CyberArk Identity as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP).

## SAML Overview

SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) enables federated authentication. CyberArk Identity acts as the IdP, authenticating users and providing SAML assertions to Service Providers (SPs) like Salesforce, AWS, and custom applications.

## Adding a SAML Application

Step 1: Navigate to Apps > Add Web App > SAML

Step 2: Configure the Service Provider settings:
- SP Entity ID (e.g., urn:amazon:webservices)
- Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL
- NameID format (email, persistent, or transient)

Step 3: Download the IdP metadata XML for the SP configuration

Step 4: Configure attribute mapping:

```xml
<Attribute Name="email">
  <AttributeValue>${user.email}</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="firstName">
  <AttributeValue>${user.firstName}</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="groups">
  <AttributeValue>${user.groups}</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
```

## Configuring MFA for SSO

Enforce multi-factor authentication before SAML assertion:

1. Navigate to the application's Authentication Policy
2. Add an MFA step:
   - TOTP authenticator
   - Push notification (CyberArk Mobile)
   - FIDO2 security key
   - SMS verification (not recommended for high-security)
3. Configure conditional MFA rules:
   - Always require MFA for admin roles
   - Risk-based MFA for standard users
   - Skip MFA from trusted networks/devices

## Common SAML Configurations

### AWS Console SSO

```json
{
  "app_type": "SAML",
  "sp_entity_id": "urn:amazon:webservices",
  "acs_url": "https://signin.aws.amazon.com/saml",
  "name_id_format": "email",
  "attributes": {
    "https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/Role": "arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/CyberArkSSO,arn:aws:iam::123456789:saml-provider/CyberArk",
    "https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/RoleSessionName": "${user.email}"
  }
}
```

### Salesforce SSO

CyberArk Identity includes a pre-built Salesforce integration:
1. Select Salesforce from the app catalog
2. Enter your Salesforce domain
3. CyberArk automatically configures endpoints and attribute mapping
4. Download the certificate and upload to Salesforce Identity Provider settings

## Troubleshooting SSO

### SAML Response Invalid
- Check clock skew between IdP and SP (must be within 5 minutes)
- Verify the certificate has not expired
- Ensure the NameID matches a valid user in the SP

### User Cannot Access Application
- Verify the user is assigned to the application in CyberArk Identity
- Check group membership and role assignments
- Review the authentication policy for blocking conditions

### Redirect Loop
- Clear browser cookies
- Verify the ACS URL is correct
- Check that the SP is not requiring additional authentication after SAML assertion

## SCIM Provisioning

Automate user provisioning alongside SSO using SCIM 2.0:
- Create/update/deactivate users in SPs automatically
- Sync group memberships
- Supported for Salesforce, AWS SSO, Slack, and 100+ applications
